item.title: Transform SQL Rows to Columns Dynamically
item.description:
“Transform SQL Rows to Columns Dynamically”

When working with relational databases, a common task is reshaping data to present it in a more readable format. Specifically, transforming multiple rows into distinct columns based on certain criteria. This is often referred to as a “pivot” or “cross-tab” operation. If the number of resulting columns is fixed, static SQL can achieve this. However, when the number of columns is not predetermined and can vary, dynamic SQL becomes the preferred approach.

item.title: SQL Dynamic Table Query Execution: Best Practices & Examples
item.description:
“SQL Dynamic Table Query Execution: Best Practices & Examples”

When working with SQL databases, particularly SQL Server, you may encounter scenarios where table or column names are not static and need to be determined at runtime. This requires the use of dynamic SQL, where the SQL statement itself is constructed as a string and then executed. Properly handling dynamic SQL is crucial for both functionality and security. Let’s delve into common challenges and effective solutions for executing queries with dynamic table or column references.
